name: The return leg of the primitives-to-IMASM cycle: reading a concatenated IMASM word back into the twelve primitive types that wrote it. The forward leg writes each type as its own program and concatenates in canonical axis order; the return leg parses the word axis by axis, each axis consuming an admissible type program as a prefix, because type programs are not self-delimiting. The reading recovers the original type at every axis but is not injective: the alphabet emits fewer distinct programs than it has types, and where two colliding types share an axis the word has two pre-images and the reading reports both rather than choosing. A mu that inverts its delta everywhere except on one axis, where the ambiguity belongs to the alphabet and not to the reading.

phase_0.boundary_condition: The concatenated IMASM word, a linear string of Shavian characters encoding the twelve primitive types in canonical axis order, serving as the closed input to the reading process.

VINIT.justification: The concatenated word before any parsing begins; a void state of interpretation where the string exists but no type has been recovered from it.

TANCH.justification: The terminal boundary of the concatenated word, signaling that all twelve axes have been consumed and the reading process is complete.

AFWD.justification: The forward morphism of the parser consuming the next admissible type program as a prefix from the remaining word, moving from one axis to the next in canonical order.

AREV.justification: When a consumed prefix admits two colliding type pre-images, the parser reverses to the axis start and reports both, descending into the ambiguity rather than resolving it.

CLINK.justification: The composition of twelve axis-parsing steps chained in canonical order, each consuming its prefix and passing the remainder to the next axis.

IMSCRIB.justification: The reading process is itself a type program in the grammar's lattice; the parser recognizes its own structural type as it reads, maintaining identity across the cycle.

FSPLIT.justification: At the axis where two types share an admissible program, the parser splits into two interpretive branches, one for each colliding pre-image, rather than committing to one.

FFUSE.justification: The two branches reconstitute the original axis input by reporting both pre-images together; the fused output is the pair of types that collided, recovering the ambiguity of the alphabet.

EVALT.justification: The affirmative state where a single type is recovered from the consumed prefix without collision, a successful deterministic parse of that axis.

EVALF.justification: The negative state where no admissible type program matches the prefix at the current axis, indicating a malformed word or corrupted input.

ENGAGR.justification: The paradice where both colliding pre-images are held simultaneously without resolution; the reading reports both types as valid interpretations of the same axis prefix.

IFIX.justification: The permanent, append-only record of the twelve recovered types, written as the output of the reading process, including any collision pairs on the ambiguous axis.

phase_3.void_description: The concatenated word before any axis has been parsed; no type has been recovered, the reading process is uninitialized.

phase_3.both_description: An axis where two colliding types share the same admissible program; both are held as valid pre-images, the ambiguity is reported rather than resolved.

phase_5.ipc_mechanism: The remainder string passed from one axis parser to the next; each axis consumes its prefix and hands the unconsumed suffix forward.
phase_5.memory_mechanism: The accumulator holding the recovered type tuple, updated axis by axis, with collision axes storing both pre-images.
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: Canonical axis order, fixed by the grammar's twelve-primitive lattice, determines the strict sequential order of parsing.
phase_5.alfs_store: The grammar's own type lattice, which defines the admissible programs for each primitive and the collision map where two types share a program.

phase_6.cycle_cost: One parse step per axis, consuming the prefix characters from the word; the collision axis costs an additional backtrack and dual-report step.

phase_6.post_cycle_state: The twelve types are recovered, with the collision axis reporting both pre-images; the word is fully consumed.
